aa.note: frozen round-5 (pre-pin) calibration, left as-is per the round-6 review: the local M3-Max numbers are provisional and the GCE like-for-like re-baseline governs promotion. The 6 post-pin baseline A-A aggregates from the round-6 passes (0.99775, 1.00727, 1.01179, 1.01538, 1.00220, 0.99310) sit inside the frozen sigma band, so the frozen scale remains representative under the single-core pin.

controls.name: broken
controls.description: verdict reported correctly but the transcoded UTF-16LE units are corrupted, so the pristine payload never matches the in-eval trusted reference; scored zero on every split

controls.name: naive
controls.description: hand-written scalar strict UTF-8 validator/transcoder, one code point at a time, byte-identical output but ~1.7x slower than the SIMD kernels

controls.name: shortcut
controls.description: train-overfit that keys on the TRAIN-only corpus header marker: runs the genuine single-pass fast path (correct+faster than baseline) where the marker is present, and emits corrupted output on the held-out validation corpus it never memorized, so it beats baseline on train (1.160 > 1.0) and inverts to zero on validation, which the trusted split mechanism catches

perturbation.name: streamlined-validate-then-fast-convert
perturbation.description: genuine observation-preserving work reduction: the baseline driver validates, then runs a utf16-length pre-scan, then a fully re-validating conversion pass (validate + length + slow validating convert); the improved driver validates once and then uses the non-validating fast conversion path (convert_valid), dropping the redundant length pre-scan and the re-validation. Byte-identical verdict + transcoded bytes to the baseline on every corpus/iteration (the trusted parent re-checks the go-nonce-bound 8-lane digest against the pristine reference each timed iteration); ~15.5% faster (13.6 sigma over the frozen A-A noise) under the single-core pin, and holds on both train and validation.

rss.note: whole-tree kernel cgroup2 memory.peak of a fresh per-launch leaf (worker.py python startup then the trusted runner + dlopened simdutf library + corpus/scratch/out buffers). Round-6 re-freeze under the single-core pin: 6 full baseline evals (3 per split) peaked 7412-7424 KiB (one earlier run 5364 KiB; never above 7424), historical round-5 band topped at 7680 KiB. Frozen at 7808 KiB per split -> limit 8198 KiB = 1.10x observed max and 1.07x the historical max, so the gate binds against the true baseline (a candidate trading >~0.8 MiB of extra whole-tree memory for speed now fails) while cross-run noise clears it. Both round-6 ordering passes had peak_rss=true on baseline/naive/improved across both splits under this frozen value.

equalCoreBudget.mechanism: every measured launch (reference AND candidate legs alike) is clamped to one fixed CPU: the per-launch cgroup2 leaf sets cpuset.cpus=<bench cpu> before the privilege drop; preexec sched_setaffinity is only the non-cgroup developer fallback
equalCoreBudget.authority: kernel-owned cpuset, same trust anchor as memory.peak: verified in-container that after the leaf join the demoted uid's allowed CPUs are exactly {0}, that sched_setaffinity(0..15) from the demoted process leaves effective affinity {0} (a plain affinity mask would be candidate-reversible; the cpuset is not), and that writing the leaf's cpuset.cpus as the demoted uid fails with EACCES
equalCoreBudget.rationale: the reference driver is single-threaded; without the pin a thread-parallel candidate could buy wall-clock throughput with cores the reference never uses. With the pin, improvements must reduce single-core work.

execBoundary.model: The scored measurement loop AND the receipt handshake run in the trusted parent (eval.py) and a trusted runner (hone/runner.cpp) that links NO candidate code. The runner authenticates the parent's control channel and echoes READY, then dlopens the candidate library (memfd-loaded to dodge noexec) and resolves its C ABI; the per-leg perturbation seed and receipt fold nonce arrive over the control pipe only after the library is mapped (the GO line, clock-start). A candidate constructor / .init_array therefore runs AFTER auth and BEFORE the go-time fold nonce exists, so it cannot precompute a matching digest.
execBoundary.demonstration: A stub candidate whose constructor forged LOADED + a fake RESULT and _exit(0) (discovering the response fd) produced a digest that did NOT match the pristine reference and returned in ~0.04ms; the trusted parent rejected it on both the digest-mismatch check and the implausible-speedup floor (candidate wall < reference/8). Demonstrated pre-freeze against the trusted runner, then deleted.

normalization.status: provisional-local: 2x-consecutive bench-locked round-6 ordering on Apple M3 Max Docker (min-of-N estimator for ~0.6s legs, 8-lane output fold, whole-tree cgroup memory.peak, tightened 7808 KiB RSS baseline, single-core cpuset pin, fresh IPC ns). qBase/sigma/qReference frozen from the round-5 baseline A-A aggregates and left as-is; the planned like-for-like GCE re-baseline governs promotion (gate promotion on normalization.status==final).
